A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same convergence-analysis work, with substantial overlap in algorithms, assumptions and proofs. All pages, including Appendices A and B, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical results and proofs. Its empirical examples and references to Padam experiments are attributed to other work; the appendices contain no original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 reports convergence theorems and proofs, including high-probability bounds. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original experiments, simulations or data analyses.

M1.justification: The retained AMSGrad and corrected RMSProp updates explicitly gain epsilon stabilization: their preconditioners change from diag(vhat_t) to diag(vhat_t + epsilon). Their momentum, moving-average and output-selection procedures remain unchanged. The shift from Padam to AdaGrad principally changes which existing optimizers receive theoretical treatment.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or concrete test scenarios. The removed DenseNet/CIFAR-10 example in v2 is attributed background motivation, not an experiment conducted by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version contains an experimental baseline comparison. Comparisons with SGD and prior adaptive-method results concern theoretical convergence bounds.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to step-size conditions, gradient assumptions and convergence criteria occur within mathematical analyses.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablation, robustness or empirical sensitivity studies. The changing discussions of partial adaptivity and gradient growth are theoretical analyses covered by T1 and C2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3's new high-probability bounds are mathematical guarantees rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries. The changed convergence rates and comparisons are formal mathematical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2's p,q-dependent Padam theorem and partial-adaptivity corollaries are replaced by epsilon-dependent AMSGrad/RMSProp bounds and new AdaGrad corollaries. v3 derives O(sqrt(d)/T^(3/4-s/2) + d/T) under a per-coordinate cumulative-gradient growth condition, retaining the earlier worst-case rate at s = 1/2. Section 6 adds a sub-Gaussian assumption and high-probability guarantees, with new martingale arguments and substantially revised proofs in Appendices A and B.

C1.justification: v2 centers on Padam and claims it is necessary for faster convergence than AMSGrad. v3 replaces this with claims of sparse-gradient advantages over SGD for AMSGrad, corrected RMSProp and AdaGrad, and first high-probability convergence guarantees. The abstract, contributions and conclusion materially change scope.

C2.justification: The explanations favoring Padam's p in [0, 1/4] and their alignment with cited experiments disappear. v3 instead interprets cumulative-gradient growth through s, discusses AMSGrad's resolution of Adam's convergence issue, and explains the relevance of high-probability guarantees to individual optimization runs.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly lists epsilon as an algorithm input and explains its numerical-stability role. Neither version provides code access, hardware information or instantiated experimental hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Padam moves from the central subject to related work; its citation is retained under the updated Chen et al. (2020) publication. v3 substantially expands adaptive-optimization and high-probability literature, including comparisons with Defossez et al. (2020) and Li and Orabona (2020). The earlier generalization-gap and DenseNet/CIFAR-10 positioning is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work and notation become separate sections, and v3 introduces distinct expectation, high-probability and proof-sketch sections while retaining detailed appendices. This substantially reorganizes the narrative and explanation of the proofs.

P2.justification: The three algorithm panels are redistributed across two pages, with Padam's panel replaced by AdaGrad and the retained panels updated. Both versions retain a similar single-column mathematical layout and contain no figures or results tables.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the proof strategy more accessible through Section 7 and adds high-probability analysis, while removing the Padam-specific theory. However, its new AdaGrad proofs in Appendices A.3 and A.6 reuse an AMSGrad argument relying on the uniform accumulator bound in Lemma A.1, which Algorithm 3's cumulative sum does not generally satisfy. This unresolved support for a central added claim prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
